T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.
T1110.detection: Monitor authentication logs for repeated failures against the same account or from the same source in a short window (e.g. multiple 'Failed password' entries in auth.log).
T1110.mitigation: Enforce account lockout thresholds, use fail2ban or similar, require MFA, and disable password-based SSH auth in favor of keys.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.tactic: Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Defense Evasion
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to evade detection.
T1078.detection: Correlate successful logins with unusual source IPs, times, or immediately following failed attempts.
T1078.mitigation: Use MFA, monitor for anomalous login patterns, and enforce least privilege on all accounts.

T1078.003.name: Valid Accounts: Local Accounts
T1078.003.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account for privilege escalation or persistence.
T1078.003.detection: Audit local group membership changes, especially additions to privileged groups like sudo/wheel.
T1078.003.mitigation: Restrict and audit local admin group membership; alert on group modification events.

T1136.001.name: Create Account: Local Account
T1136.001.description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems.
T1136.001.detection: Monitor for useradd/groupadd invocations and new entries in /etc/passwd, /etc/group, and auth.log.
T1136.001.mitigation: Restrict account creation to authorized administrators and alert on new local account creation.

T1222.002.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification
T1222.002.description: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists or allow further actions.
T1222.002.mitigation: Monitor chmod/chown invocations on sensitive paths and use file integrity monitoring.
T1222.002.detection: Watch syslog/auditd for chmod, chown, and setfacl calls against sensitive paths.

T1053.003.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
T1053.003.description: Adversaries may abuse cron to execute programs at system startup or on a schedule for persistence.
T1053.003.detection: Review crontab -l for all users, and monitor /etc/cron.* and /var/spool/cron for unexpected entries.
T1053.003.mitigation: Restrict crontab access, monitor changes to cron directories, and alert on new/edited jobs.

T1005.name: Data from Local System
T1005.description: Adversaries may search local file systems for files of interest prior to exfiltration.
T1005.detection: Monitor file access patterns and creation of files in temp/staging directories.
T1005.mitigation: Apply least-privilege file permissions and monitor sensitive directories with FIM tooling.

DS0028.name: Logon Session (Detection Data Source)
DS0028.description: Data generated from user logon/logoff activity, such as auth.log or Windows Security Event logs.
DS0028.detection: Ingest and correlate logon session data centrally (e.g. SIEM) for anomaly detection.
DS0028.mitigation: N/A - this is a detection data source rather than an adversary technique.

DS0002.name: User Account (Detection Data Source)
DS0002.description: Data generated from user account activities, including account creation, modification, and deletion.
DS0002.detection: Continuously audit /etc/passwd, /etc/group, and account management log events.
DS0002.mitigation: N/A - this is a detection data source rather than an adversary technique.

DS0022.name: File (Detection Data Source)
DS0022.description: Data generated from file system activity, including creation, modification, permission and ownership changes.
DS0022.detection: Enable auditd file watches (auditctl -w) on sensitive paths and forward events to a SIEM.
DS0022.mitigation: N/A - this is a detection data source rather than an adversary technique.

DS0003.name: Scheduled Job (Detection Data Source)
DS0003.description: Data generated from scheduled job activity, such as cron or systemd timer creation and execution.
DS0003.detection: Periodically diff crontabs and cron.d contents against a known-good baseline.
DS0003.mitigation: N/A - this is a detection data source rather than an adversary technique.
